Class ImportController

java.lang.Object
com.sebastiandorata.musicdashboard.controller.ImportController
@Controller public class ImportController extends Object
Web entry point for all import functionality (the desktop "Import Music" screen).

The desktop offered two workflows that both fed ImportOrchestrator: pick a folder with the DirectoryChooser and press Start Scan, or drop files/folders on a drop zone. On the web the same two entry points exist: POST /api/import/scan imports a folder that lives on the machine running the app (files stay where they are), and POST /api/import/upload receives files from the browser, stores them under the configured upload folder and imports them. Both return a job id immediately; the page polls GET /api/import/jobs/{jobId} to drive the progress bar and the results table.

SRP: translates HTTP requests into orchestrator calls and job lookups; the pipeline itself lives in ImportOrchestrator and the progress bookkeeping in ImportJobRegistry.

DIP: depends on the orchestrator and the registry abstractions, holds no per-user state.

    • upload

      @PostMapping("/api/import/upload") @ResponseBody public ImportController.JobStarted upload(org.springframework.web.multipart.MultipartHttpServletRequest request)
      Receives files chosen or dropped in the browser, stores them and starts importing them.

      Multipart fields: files (repeated, the audio files) and paths (repeated, parallel to files: the relative path of each file, for example Album/01 Song.mp3). Files are stored under <musicdashboard.upload-dir>/<userId>/<relative path> so an album stays in one folder and re-uploading a file lands on the same path. Non-audio files are ignored.

      Parameters:
      request - the multipart request
      Returns:
      the id of the new job
      Throws:
      org.springframework.web.server.ResponseStatusException - BAD_REQUEST for an unsafe path, 500 when a file cannot be stored
